newsitem.title: UK: British bank stocks to gain on rate rise - analysts.
newsitem.headline: British bank stocks to gain on rate rise - analysts.

text.p: British banking stocks, buoyant for the past few weeks, were fired up by Friday's quarter point hike in official U.K. interest rates that will swell bank profits and bolster shares, analysts said.
"The impact of the rate news is that margins will widen and that is good for lenders," said one London banking analyst.

"We've seen time and again that rate hikes allow lenders to re-price assets and liabilities in an asymmetric and advantageous fashion -- the lending rate goes up tomorrow, while saving rates are grudgingly increased later and by less," he added.

The Bank of England earlier raised interest rates to 6.50 from 6.25 percent, followed almost immediately by Abbey National Plc and Halifax Plc who both pushed their mortgage rates 35 basis points higher.

ABN Amro Hoare Govett's Peter Toeman felt the Abbey's decision to raise its mortgage rate by more than the rise in official rates signalled that it was assembling a war-chest with which to fight the newly floated Halifax for retail savings.
"They've tried to push up mortgage rates faster...to collect fire power to do more with the retail savings market," he said.
Halifax's entrance into the banking market is expected to intensify the fight for private savings.
Mounting competition may cap banks' ability to widen their lending margins and some analysts disagreed the rate hike was an licence for banks to 'print more money'.
Goldman Sachs's David Townshend said banks were desperate to raise mortgage rates by more than their wholesale cost of borrowing because margins had already been sorely pressed.
"Personally I don't think margins have much scope to rise. Competition continues and that's the reality of the market in which they operate."

British bank shares have had a roaring time of late, with the FTSE All Share Bank Index .FTBK outpacing the underlying market by almost 20 percent since the start of the year, according to Reuters 3000.
